post.caption: Tahitian black pearls are not truly black. They grow in the black-lipped pearl oyster of French Polynesia, and colors run from charcoal gray and silver to green and brown. Peacock often means green with a pink overtone. Most are about 9 to 13 millimeters across, and the oyster needs about 18 to 24 months to grow each pearl. Legend says the god Oro brought a black pearl down a rainbow. In the early 1960s, a vet had technicians graft about 5,000 oysters, and the first commercial farm opened on Manihi atoll in 1966. Dealers began selling them on world markets in the early 1970s.
